headline: Wildlife Refuge Entry and Camping Permits
reservation: Entrance to the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge is generally open, but camping at Doris Campground requires advanced booking through official federal systems. Guided wildlife tours and specific backcountry access points may use a lottery or seasonal reservation window; check the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service site for current protocols. Medicine Park accommodation is private and often requires booking months in advance for peak spring and fall periods.

days.title: Granite Peaks and Prairie Vistas

stops.name: Mount Scott
stops.detail: Drive the winding road to the summit for panoramic views of the Oklahoma plains and Lake Lawtonka.

stops.name: Holy City of the Wichitas
stops.detail: Visit this unique historic site featuring stone architecture set against the rugged mountain backdrop.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour total for the summit drive and local transfers; conditions vary.
days.note: Mount Scott road may close to vehicles during high winds or for pedestrian-only hours; check local schedules.

days.title: Ancient Canyons and Wilderness

stops.name: Charon's Garden Wilderness Area
stops.detail: Hike among massive granite boulders and rugged terrain to find hidden gems like Post Oak Falls.

stops.name: Forty-Foot Hole
stops.detail: Observe the unique geological formations where the creek has carved deep pools into the canyon rock.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for interior refuge roads; strictly observe speed limits for wildlife.
days.note: Boulder scrambling in Charon's Garden is strenuous; allow more time than mileage suggests.

days.title: Wildlife Corridors and Cobblestones

stops.name: Parallel Forest
stops.detail: Walk through a dense, unnaturally straight grid of cedars planted for government research in the early 20th century.

stops.name: Medicine Park Cobblestone Resort
stops.detail: Explore the historic resort town's unique round-stone architecture and riverside trails.

days.driving: Allow 30–40 minutes; watch for bison and longhorn cattle on the roadway.
days.note: Maintain at least 25 yards from all wildlife, especially bison and longhorn cattle.

intel.title: Dog Run Hollow Crowds
intel.text: Parking lots at popular trailheads like Dog Run Hollow fill by mid-morning on weekends. Use the smaller pull-offs along the main road if the primary lots are marked full.

intel.title: Refuge Dead Zones
intel.text: Cell service is non-existent in deep canyons like Charon's Garden. Obtain a physical map at the Visitor Center near the intersection of Hwy 49 and 115.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: No fuel or food services exist within the refuge boundaries. Fill your tank in Lawton or Medicine Park before entering the refuge gates.

intel.title: Heat Management
intel.text: Summer temperatures often exceed 100 degrees Fahrenheit; plan all hiking for the first three hours after sunrise. The granite rocks retain heat long after the sun sets.

intel.title: Seasonal Rut Closures
intel.text: Certain backcountry areas may be closed during the elk rut in October to protect wildlife and visitors. Check the official refuge portal for current area restrictions.

plan.arrival: Arrive at LAW airport and drive 30 minutes to Medicine Park for check-in before heading to the Refuge Visitor Center for trail maps.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for the main paved roads, including Mount Scott; check for height/width restrictions on narrower refuge drives.
plan.goldenHour: Mount Scott provides the most famous sunset perspective, though the road may close to vehicles shortly after dark.
